category_title: Emotionally disturbed primary student with trauma-related behavioral outbursts
student_description: Jamal is a first-grade student who exhibits severe emotional distress, trauma-related task resistance, and attention-seeking behaviors when faced with basic academic tasks. He uniquely requires consistent one-on-one relationship building, arts-based interventions (like drawing and photo elicitation), and positive visual behavior tracking, while exclusionary discipline (sending him away) completely fails.

criteria.rationale: Because exclusionary discipline fails for Jamal, he requires dedicated, non-academic time with an adult to build a secure attachment and feel safe at school.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include frequent, dedicated one-on-one time (e.g., during lunch, after school, or designated breaks) to build trust, explicitly avoiding exclusionary discipline like sending him out of the room.

criteria.rationale: Jamal's severe task resistance to traditional academics is mitigated when tasks leverage his spatial intelligence and preference for art.
criteria.check: The plan must incorporate visual arts, drawing, painting, or spatial activities as a primary method for engaging the student in learning or expression.

criteria.rationale: Given his underlying trauma regarding his family, Jamal needs safe, structured ways to process and share his personal life story.
criteria.check: The plan must include structured opportunities for the student to share personal stories or family photographs (e.g., photo elicitation or life-story splicing) to foster emotional connection.

criteria.rationale: Jamal responds exceptionally well to clear, visual systems that allow him to earn high-level positive recognition rather than just avoiding punishment.
criteria.check: The plan must implement a multi-level, visual (e.g., color-coded) behavior tracking system that emphasizes positive achievement tiers rather than solely punitive measures.
